trial_court: Court of Sh. Abhishek Goyal, Additional Sessions Judge-03, Central District, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi (CNR No.: DLCT01-016855-2024, CRIMINAL APPEAL No.: 436/2024)
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Appellant no. 1 initiated a proceeding under DV Act by filing a complaint/petition under Section 12 of DV Act before the Ld. Trial Court against respondent and his family members. The trial court awarded interim maintenance to the tune of Rs. 20,000/- per month in favour of respondent no. 2/for the minor son of appellant no. 1 and the respondent, however, declined to grant interim maintenance in favour of appellant no. 1.

legal_principles.principle: A party cannot take advantage of their own wrong.
legal_principles.held: It was asserted by the Ld. Counsel that even appellant no. 1's assertion/allegations of cruelty, etc., are grossly misconceived, rather, it was appellant no. 1, who is guilty of committing domestic violence against the respondent, leading to respondent being compelled to file a petition for divorce.
cited_cases: Shikha Singh & Anr. v. Saurabh Singh

legal_principles.principle: A party's financial status must be disclosed accurately.
legal_principles.held: Appellant no. 1, deliberately, intentionally and with ulterior motives of hiding her financial status, filed a false income and expenditure affidavit, thereby showing herself to be a destitute lady despite being a highly qualified/educated (MBA), well capable of earning, despite having enormous amount of Rs. 25,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs only) lying in her six Bank accounts.
cited_cases: Shikha Singh & Anr. v. Saurabh Singh

outcome.final_order: The court granted interim maintenance to the tune of Rs. 20,000/- per month in favour of respondent no. 2/for the minor son of appellant no. 1 and the respondent.

keywords: Protection of Women from DV Act
use_for_drafting: representing clients in maintenance and alimony disputes
